definitions.Description: The total area of the HUC12 in square meters. Calculated from a 30-meter resolution grid of HUC12 polygons in the NHDPlus2 WBD Snapshot, EnviroAtlas Version (February 2015 version). See also WBD Snapshot, EnviroAtlas Version glossary definition.
Mean elevation in the HUC12 (in feet). Source data was the NHDPlus2 National Elevation Dataset (NED) Snapshot. See also NED Snapshot glossary definition.
Minimum elevation in the HUC12 (in feet). Source data was the NHDPlus2 National Elevation Dataset (NED) Snapshot. See also NED Snapshot glossary definition.
Maximum elevation in the HUC12 (in feet). Source data was the NHDPlus2 National Elevation Dataset (NED) Snapshot. See also NED Snapshot glossary definition.
Mean slope in the HUC12 (in degrees). Source data was the NHDPlus2 National Elevation Dataset (NED) Snapshot. See also NED Snapshot glossary definition.

Percent of the HUC12 classified as forest cover by the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) 2019 Land Cover dataset (June 4, 2021 version; https://www.mrlc.gov/data/nlcd-2019-land-cover-conus). Forest cover classes include 'Deciduous Forest' (code 41), 'Evergreen Forest' (code 42), and 'Mixed Forest' (code 43) in the NLCD 2019 Land Cover dataset. Calculated as Forest area divided by HUC12 area, multiplied by 100.

Percent of the HUC12 classified as wetland cover by the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) 2019 Land Cover dataset (June 4, 2021 version; https://www.mrlc.gov/data/nlcd-2019-land-cover-conus). Wetland cover classes include 'Woody Wetlands' (code 90), and 'Emergent Herbaceous Wetlands' (code 95) in the NLCD 2019 Land Cover dataset. Calculated as wetland area divided by HUC12 area, multiplied by 100.

Percent of the HUC12 classified as 'Shrub/Scrub' (code 52) by the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) 2019 Land Cover dataset (June 4, 2021 version; https://www.mrlc.gov/data/nlcd-2019-land-cover-conus). Calculated as 'Shrub/Scrub' area divided by HUC12 area, multiplied by 100.

Percent of the HUC12 classified as 'Grassland/Herbaceous' (code 71) by the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) 2019 Land Cover dataset (June 4, 2021 version; https://www.mrlc.gov/data/nlcd-2019-land-cover-conus). Calculated as 'Grassland/Herbaceous' area divided by HUC12 area, multiplied by 100.

Percent of the HUC12 classified as 'Open Water' (code 11) by the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) 2019 Land Cover dataset (June 4, 2021 version; https://www.mrlc.gov/data/nlcd-2019-land-cover-conus). Calculated as 'Open Water' area divided by HUC12 area, multiplied by 100.

Percent of the HUC12 classified as 'Barren Land (Rock/Sand/Clay)' (code 31) by the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) 2019 Land Cover dataset (June 4, 2021 version; https://www.mrlc.gov/data/nlcd-2019-land-cover-conus). Calculated as 'Barren Land (Rock/Sand/Clay)' area divided by HUC12 area, multiplied by 100.

definitions.Indicator_Name: % Low Runoff Potential Soils in HUC12
definitions.Description: Percent of the HUC12 containing soils classified as having low potential for surface runoff. Soils with low runoff potential are assigned to Hydrologic Soil Group A and are defined as having a high rate of infiltration when thoroughly wet. They consist mainly of deep, well-drained sands. Source data was the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) Gridded Soil Survey Geographic (gSSURGO) database (July 2020 version; https://nrcs.app.box.com/v/gateway/folder/119454159836). Calculated for each HUC12 as: Area of Hydrologic Soil Group A in HUC12 / HUC12 Area * 100. HUC12s were assigned a blank value if soil runoff potential was not reported for more than 50% of the HUC12 land area.

definitions.Indicator_Name: % Moderately Low Runoff Potential Soils in HUC12
definitions.Description: Percent of the HUC12 containing soils classified as having moderately low potential for surface runoff. Soils with moderately low runoff potential are assigned to Hydrologic Soil Group B and are defined as having a moderate rate of infiltration. They consist mainly of moderately deep, moderately well-drained soils, with grain textures between moderately fine to moderately coarse. Source data was the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) Gridded Soil Survey Geographic (gSSURGO) database (July 2020 Version; https://nrcs.app.box.com/v/gateway/folder/119454159836). Calculated for each HUC12 as: Area of Hydrologic Soil Group B in HUC12 / HUC12 Area * 100. HUC12s were assigned a blank value if soil runoff potential was not reported for more than 50% of the HUC12 land area.

Percent of the HUC12 classified as urban cover by the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) 2019 Land Cover dataset (June 4, 2021 version; https://www.mrlc.gov/data/nlcd-2019-land-cover-conus). Urban cover classes include 'Developed, Open Space' (code 21), 'Developed, Low Intensity' (code 22), 'Developed, Medium Intensity' (code 23), 'Developed, High Intensity' (code 24) in the NLCD 2019 Land Cover dataset. Calculated as urban area divided by HUC12 area, multiplied by 100.

definitions.Indicator_Name: % Moderately High Runoff Potential Soils in HUC12
definitions.Description: Percent of the HUC12 containing soils classified as having moderately high potential for surface runoff. Soils with moderately high runoff potential are assigned to Hydrologic Soil Group C and are defined as having a slow rate of infiltration. They consist mainly of soils having a layer that impedes the downward movement of water or soils with a moderately fine or fine texture. Source data was the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) Gridded Soil Survey Geographic (gSSURGO) database (July 2020 Version; https://nrcs.app.box.com/v/gateway/folder/119454159836). Calculated for each HUC12 as: Area of Hydrologic Soil Group C in HUC12 / HUC12 Area * 100. HUC12s were assigned a blank value if soil runoff potential was not reported for more than 50% of the HUC12 land area.

definitions.Indicator_Name: % High Runoff Potential Soils in HUC12
definitions.Description: Percent of the HUC12 containing soils classified as having high potential for surface runoff. Soils with high runoff potential are assigned to Hydrologic Soil Group D and are defined as having a very slow rate of infiltration. They consist mainly of clays that have a high shrink-swell potential, a high water table, a claypan or clay layer at or near the surface, and/or are shallow over the top of nearly impervious material. Source data was the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) Gridded Soil Survey Geographic (gSSURGO) database (July 2020 Version; https://nrcs.app.box.com/v/gateway/folder/119454159836). Calculated for each HUC12 as: Area of Hydrologic Soil Group D in HUC12 / HUC12 Area * 100. HUC12s were assigned a blank value if soil runoff potential was not reported for more than 50% of the HUC12 land area.
